findings.description: The inline policy grants ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, and cloudwatch:* on Resource "*", giving this user full administrative control across four services. This includes the ability to read/modify every S3 object, alter IAM-adjacent compute config, and destroy data, so any compromise of this identity is effectively an account-wide breach (privilege escalation / broken access control).

This output emits access key material for the svc_deploy user and is not marked sensitive = true, so the value is rendered in CLI output and stored in plaintext in Terraform state/logs. Combined with the wildcard policy attached to this user, disclosure of this value yields broad account access.

A permanent IAM user access key is created (with no PGP encryption of the secret, so the plaintext secret is also persisted in state). Static keys tied to a user with wildcard permissions do not rotate and provide a durable, non-expiring credential for an over-privileged identity; temporary role credentials would be the secure alternative.
